messages:
Alex: quick heads-up, ran a pass on the fallback compatibility matrix and found a few subtle but real gaps between model variants that could break graceful routing. :eyes:
Maria: can you list the gaps you saw? high level is fine, we can triage.
Alex: sure — main categories: tokenizer normalization mismatch (utf8 vs byte-bpe), context-limit behavior (truncation vs error), and tool-calling parity (different arg schemas / required fields). also some variants shuffle kv cache layout which breaks our prefix-caching assumptions.
Sam: ugh the kv layout one is nasty. do you have an example where a fallback model actually fails the cached session?
Alex: yes — session id 19fc used rtx-variant-A then fell back to v-small which uses different kv ordering; result was out-of-order completions and tool-call desync.
Jia: for tokenizer, are we seeing different token counts for the same prompt or different normalization (NFC vs NFD)? that changes rollouts significantly.
Alex: both. one variant's tokenizer returns 2 extra tokens because it treats U+200D sequences differently. another does NFC folding so comparisons fail.
Maria: does this mean we need an explicit per-variant "normalization" column in the matrix? like: normalization=NFC/NFD, byte_bpe=true/false, special_tokens_map version.
Sam: yes. and add a "tool-call schema" column: signature-hash + required-fields list. we had a fallback that ignored a required `user_id` field and pipeline crashed.
Jia: proposal: extend the matrix with these columns and a short compatibility status: exact/parity/partial/incompatible. also add a "mitigation" note (e.g., auto-transform, recommend-model, disallow-fallback).
Alex: +1. Also we should surface this in Console rollout UX — when configuring a canary, warn if selected fallback variants are marked partial/incompatible for that customer's tier/region.
Maria: agree. for quotas: some tiers have per-token budgeting that assumes strict token accounting; if tokenizer differs, billing and alerts mismatch. need telemetry flag that tags token_source_variant to each request.
OpsAnalytics: noted — we can emit a new telemetry field `tokenizer_variant` and `token_count_method` so billing and dashboards can reconcile. will prototype a schema.
Sam: for tool-calling parity, we should include a small sample mapping in the matrix instead of full proto — like `calls_like: modelX:v1 -> required: [user_id, session_pos]` and a short sample payload.
Alex: sample snippet I used to reproduce:
```
payload = {
  "func": "charge_user",
  "args": {"user_id": 123, "amount": 9.99},
  "schema_version": "svc-v2"
}
```
Fallback model stripped `schema_version` and returned `400` from our adapter.
Maria: ok action items: 1) Jia + OpsAnalytics update matrix columns and telemetry schema, 2) Sam + Eng-API add console warning for incompatible fallback combos, 3) Alex to add a short repro doc and attach failing session ids. anyone volunteering to own a quick spike to run automated parity tests? 48h spike ideally.
Jia: I can own the matrix + telemetry spike. will push a PR with new CSV and example rows.
Sam: I'll do the console warning — will stub the UX modal text and add a backend flag check.
Alex: I'll drop repro logs in the incident board and link the session ids.
deploy-bot: Canary rule `fallback-safe-checks` deployed to eu-west-1 (id=fallback-canary-2026-04). Monitor latency/regressions for 2h.
Maria: thanks. one more thing — region-tier routing: for PREMIUM tier we want fallback to prefer variants with exact parity even if cost slightly higher. for BASIC tier we allow partial parity but block tool-calls. can we express that in the routing policy layer?
Sam: yes, policy DSL already supports `prefer_exact=true` and `deny_on_tool_mismatch=true`. we need to make these toggles visible in Console when editing routing rules.
Jia: I'll add example rows showing policy effects in the matrix PR so product can review.
Maria: perfect. last ask: please keep messages succinct in the PR — product wants a one-line summary per row plus the raw sample when available.
Alex: got it. thanks all :thumbsup:
